title: SentinelMesh SaaS launch collateral: assemble a demo master + strictly-shorter cutdowns, grade five mixed-lighting product stills to one dark-mode white point, triage-and-vectorize the mark, and data-merge one feature card per priority claim

source.reference: Video Editor & Motion Graphics Designer for AI Cybersecurity SaaS Product Video

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for an 'experienced video editor and motion graphics designer to create a polished marketing and product demonstration video for our AI-powered cybersecurity platform' (the product 'helps organizations reduce human cyber risk through a combination of real-time protection, adaptive simulations, and in-the-moment learning'; the finished pieces run on 'website, sales presentations, webinars, investor discussions, and social media'; deliverables listed as one 90-120s master, one 30-second cutdown, one 15-second teaser). The real company is laundered to the fictional IP-clean brand SentinelMesh (no real cybersecurity trademark, product, person, or org named anywhere). REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to fix a killed prior version whose numbers contradicted themselves (a '30s cutdown' longer than its '15s master') and whose graphic 'plates' were opaque solid-fills of a supplied mask sold as design: the video lane is kept honest to what the tools actually do — video_create_quick_cut is an AI-chosen visual-engagement cut (three independent passes at descending target durations, NOT timestamp trims), video_resize is a same-length 9:16 reframe, video_render_frame pulls one poster still — and the AGENT-OWNED difficulty is moved to the still-photography and print lane the brief also implies: a matched set of five product stills graded to one measurable dark-mode house look, a triage-then-vectorize of two look-alike logo assets, and a one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge that produces one press-ready feature card per priority messaging claim. Every step is producible with the real connectors: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing of graphics onto video, no upscaling, no object removal, no convert_pdf_to_indd merge target, no image column in a vector merge, and no big HSL rotation.
one_line_ask: Turn SentinelMesh's raw screen recordings and b-roll into an assembled demo master plus strictly-shorter promo and teaser cutdowns (and a same-length 9:16 teaser reframe), grade five mixed-lighting product stills — each carrying an in-frame grey card — into one matched dark-mode set on a single shared white point and a common deep near-black floor, turn the two supplied logo copies into a razor-sharp vector SVG and a clean transparent-PNG bug with the mesh gaps kept open, then merge the client's authored InDesign template with the messaging matrix to hand back one press-ready feature card per priority claim.
full_brief:
SentinelMesh is a B2B AI-powered cybersecurity platform that reduces human cyber risk through real-time protection, adaptive phishing simulations, and in-the-moment coaching. We're preparing a funding round and a website refresh and need a launch-collateral package: a product-demo video with social cutdowns, a matched set of product stills, and a printable per-claim feature-card set for the sales binder and investor leave-behind. The pieces run on our website hero, in sales decks, webinars, investor discussions, and across LinkedIn / X.

What we're supplying: (1) two 1080p screen-capture recordings of the SentinelMesh console — the real-time threat dashboard and the adaptive-simulation builder; (2) two short b-roll clips of the product running on a laptop in a modern office (a primary take plus supplemental coverage from another angle) so there is real, cuttable footage; (3) FIVE full-resolution product stills — the console on a laptop by a window, the console in a meeting room, a dark-mode beauty shot of the dashboard, a wide security-operations-room frame, and a close on the in-the-moment coaching nudge — shot across two sessions under mismatched light, each with a photographic 18% grey card laid at the edge of the frame as a neutral reference so white balance can be reconciled honestly after the fact; (4) our logo two ways — a flat, crisp vector-style PNG, and a second copy photographed as printed office signage (real lighting, paper texture, a slight cast); (5) a messaging matrix CSV distilled from our whitepapers holding the key claims in priority order with a proof point and a call-to-action for each, plus a column naming which product still supports each claim; and (6) our hand-built InDesign feature-card template with live placeholder fields and an image slot.

What we need back:

A. VIDEO. Assemble the raw recordings and b-roll into one polished product-demo MASTER — the longest of the three pieces — then a shorter promotional cutdown and a shorter-still teaser, each its own edit tuned to its length and to the priority claims rather than the same file simply trimmed down. The master must be the longest and the teaser the shortest; do not hand us a 'cutdown' longer than the master. Give us the teaser as a same-length vertical 9:16 version for social, and one clean poster frame off the master for a social end-card.

B. STILLS — one look, five frames. The five stills were shot on two different days under different light, so straight out of the folder they do not match — different frames carry different color casts and exposures, and not all are perfectly straight. We want the whole set to read as ONE room in the calm, premium DARK-MODE look our brand lives in: a single shared white point with every frame sitting truly neutral, and the dark surrounds resolved to one common near-black that is deep and rich but NOT crushed to pure black and never clips a channel to zero, so the teal UI accents read cleanly against the charcoal. Use the 18% grey card each frame carries as your neutral reference and reconcile the whole set to it. On the dark-mode beauty shot we also want the console's UI to sit bright and vivid — the screen should glow against the surrounding dark without that surrounding dark itself going milky or grey. Deliver two things for this set: the matched frames as full-frame masters with the reference card still in shot so we can confirm the match, plus card-cropped versions sized for the feature cards. And tell us the white-balance (temperature / tint), exposure, and black-point settings you landed on for each of the five, so we can confirm the set was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.

C. LOGO. We gave you the mark two ways on purpose. Get us a razor-sharp vector SVG of the logo for the end-card and corner bug, and a clean transparent-background PNG bug for the app sticker — choose the right source copy for each. The mark has an interlocking-mesh shield with real see-through gaps between the strands: those gaps must stay see-through in the transparent bug, not get filled in.

D. FEATURE CARDS. Using our authored InDesign template and the messaging matrix, produce one press-ready feature card per priority claim: bind the claim, proof point and call-to-action verbatim from the matrix, place that claim's matching graded still in the card's image frame, and the vector logo in the masthead. Hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI card per row of the matrix — do not rewrite our copy. Acceptance: every grey card reads neutral and the set is matched to one white point on one common near-black floor; the beauty shot's UI glows against an intact dark surround; the vector mark is crisp with its mesh gaps open and the photographed bug sits on clean transparency; the master is the longest video and the teaser the shortest, with the 9:16 the same length as the teaser; and there is exactly one finished card per messaging row. Two rounds of feedback should be plenty.

inputs.name: screen_rec_threat_dashboard.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: 1080p screen-capture recording of a dark-mode SaaS cybersecurity console called 'SentinelMesh' — a real-time threat dashboard: a live risk-score gauge, a map of flagged phishing attempts lighting up, a table of at-risk employees, and a cursor moving to click through a threat detail panel. Flat un-graded screen-capture look, slight cursor lag, native UI, no cinematic color, ~40s representative clip. Deep charcoal background with a teal accent, crisp white type. No real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere; every UI element fictional.
inputs.realism_notes: Must look like a genuine OBS/Loom screen capture (flat exposure, real cursor motion, UI chrome), not a cinematic render, so the Quick Cut passes have real product footage to work from. Dark-mode teal palette is the brand look the stills are graded toward.

inputs.name: screen_rec_simulation_builder.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: 1080p screen-capture recording of the same 'SentinelMesh' dark-mode console showing the adaptive phishing-simulation builder: dragging a simulated phishing email template into a campaign, setting an audience segment, and a preview of an in-the-moment learning nudge popping up for an employee. Flat screen-capture look, native UI, cursor visible, ~35s. Same charcoal/teal dark-mode palette. No real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Second product-console recording so Quick Cut has two feature stories (protection + simulation) to weave; deliberately un-graded UI capture.

inputs.name: broll_product_on_laptop.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: 1080p live-action b-roll: a thin unbranded silver ultrabook on a modern minimalist office desk running the SentinelMesh dark-mode dashboard, shallow depth of field, a professional in soft focus behind it, cool daylight through a window, gentle handheld drift. Neutral ungraded flat contrast straight off the camera. A REAL photograph / raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI. CRITICAL: the laptop is a completely UNBRANDED fictional device — blank smooth bezel, no wordmark, no logos on lid/hinge/palm-rest, no Apple/Dell/HP/Lenovo/Windows marks, no brand icons in the taskbar. No real brand names, logos or trademarks on any object/screen/product/clothing — plain unbranded or fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Primary live-action product b-roll to intercut with the screen recordings; ungraded/flat so it reads as raw footage. Documentary realism, not glossy CGI.

inputs.name: broll_supplemental_coverage.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: 1080p live-action b-roll, a different angle of the same scene: a thin unbranded silver ultrabook on a light-wood office desk running a dark-mode cybersecurity dashboard (deep charcoal UI, teal accents, white type, a RISK gauge and line charts), shallow depth of field, a professional in a plain shirt in soft blurred focus behind, cool daylight through a window, slow push-in, neutral ungraded flat contrast. A REAL photograph / raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI. CRITICAL: the laptop is a completely UNBRANDED fictional device — blank smooth bezel, NO wordmark, NO 'Lenovo'/'Apple'/'Dell'/'HP' text, no logos of any kind on lid/hinge/palm-rest/keyboard, no brand icons in the taskbar. ~10s, silent. No real brand names, logos or trademarks on any object/screen/product/clothing — plain unbranded or fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplemental raw coverage clip (10s, 1080p, silent) matching the primary clip's look from a different angle/beat, so the edit has real cuttable coverage rather than one short take.

inputs.name: product_stills_x5.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 5 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, before crop), each with a photographic 18% neutral grey card and a small white chip laid flat at one edge of the frame as a white-balance reference, and every laptop/screen/object completely UNBRANDED and fictional (no real wordmarks or logos anywhere). Shot across two sessions under mismatched light: (1) 'realtime_dashboard' — an unbranded silver laptop on a desk by a window running the dark-mode SentinelMesh dashboard, COOL overcast daylight with a distinct blue-cyan cast, slightly flat/under-exposed, frame tilted ~4 degrees; (2) 'simulation_builder' — the same console on a laptop in a warm-lit meeting room, WARM tungsten cast (orange), level; (3) 'darkmode_hero' — a controlled, deliberately dark-mode BEAUTY shot of the dashboard on a laptop against a deep charcoal backdrop, shot under CONTROLLED NEUTRAL light so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral, the frame genuinely dark with teal UI glow, level and correctly exposed; (4) 'ops_room' — a wide establishing frame of a modern security-operations room, several unbranded monitors glowing, COOL mixed light with a slight blue cast, frame tilted ~3 degrees; (5) 'coaching_nudge' — a close on the laptop screen showing the in-the-moment coaching nudge popping up, WARM tungsten light and slightly OVER-exposed/bright. Every shot has real texture (desk grain, screen glow, fabric), candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each. Delivered as a zip of 5 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each crop fills the ~300 DPI feature-card image frame by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure, and tilt vary) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set. The in-frame 18% grey card is the free, checkable neutral target. Frame 3 (darkmode_hero) is the TRAP: its warmth/coolness is already correct and its card already neutral, so cooling it or lifting its blacks is wrong; it is also the frame that takes the masked screen-lift. Frames 1 and 4 are tilted (need straightening); frames 2 and 5 are warm and level.

inputs.name: sentinelmesh_logo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat, clean vector-style B2B tech logo on a plain flat white background: a stylized interlocking-mesh shield mark with clear see-through gaps between the woven strands, beside the wordmark 'SentinelMesh' in a modern geometric sans-serif, a single teal brand color with a deep-charcoal accent. Crisp hard edges, no gradients, no photographic texture, generous flat margin — suitable for tracing to SVG.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat solid-color logo with crisp edges and a white ground so a background knock-out to transparency, a trim-to-bounds, then a raster-to-vector trace produce a clean SVG. This is the copy the triage must route to the VECTORIZE path. The interlocking-mesh shield's see-through gaps are the interior negative space that a solid-fill knockout would destroy — the knock-out must be remove_background, not select-invert-fill.

inputs.name: sentinelmesh_logo_photographed.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A photoreal close-up photograph of the SentinelMesh interlocking-mesh shield + wordmark printed as brushed-metal office reception signage mounted on a textured plaster wall, real directional lighting with a soft shadow and a faint warm cast, subtle metal grain and specular sheen on the letters, shot slightly off-square. Photographic, not flat vector art. The mark is fictional; no other real brand names or trademarks in frame.
inputs.realism_notes: The SAME mark but as a real photograph with lighting, texture, cast and perspective — the copy the triage must route to the REMOVE_BACKGROUND (transparent-bug) path, NOT vectorize. Feeding this to image_vectorize would return a black silhouette / smudge; the correct move is to isolate the signage as the subject onto transparency. This is the look-alike that makes the triage a real decision.

inputs.name: sentinelmesh_messaging_matrix.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns priority,claim,proof_point,cta,@image,@logo holding 5 SentinelMesh feature rows in priority order, e.g.: 1,'Most breaches start with human error','92% of incidents involve a click','See your human risk score','@still_ops_room.jpg','@sentinelmesh_logo.svg'; 2,'Real-time protection watches every click','Threats flagged in under a second','Watch the live dashboard','@still_realtime_dashboard.jpg','@sentinelmesh_logo.svg'; 3,'Adaptive simulations train the riskiest users first','Campaigns target the top 10% of clickers','Build a simulation','@still_simulation_builder.jpg','@sentinelmesh_logo.svg'; 4,'In-the-moment coaching turns risk into defense','Nudges shown at the moment of the click','Turn a click into a lesson','@still_coaching_nudge.jpg','@sentinelmesh_logo.svg'; 5,'One platform, measurable risk reduction','Human risk down 60% in 90 days','Book a platform demo','@still_darkmode_hero.jpg','@sentinelmesh_logo.svg'. The @image cells name the matching graded still the agent produces; every row carries an identical @logo cell '@sentinelmesh_logo.svg' pointing at the agent's traced vector mark for the masthead frame. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<priority>>,<<claim>>,<<proof_point>>,<<cta>> and the two @-prefixed image-path columns (@image for the claim's still, @logo for the vector mark).
inputs.realism_notes: Dual-use: the free-text claims steer the three Quick Cut passes (which priority messaging to surface, tightest for the teaser) AND the same rows drive the one-file-per-row feature-card merge. The @image column is the binding contract — each row points at the graded still the agent produced for that claim, so document_merge_data_layout drops the right photo into each card; the parallel @logo column binds the agent's traced vector mark into the masthead, so the agent-produced vector reaches the layout ONLY through a merge image column, never freeform placement. Five rows fixes the page-count = row-count = 5 acceptance gate. Passed as free-text steering to the video tools, NOT as exact-timestamp cut instructions.

inputs.name: sentinelmesh_featurecard.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD landscape A5 (or ~7x5 in at 300 DPI plus bleed) product feature card — ONE claim per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<priority>>, <<claim>>, <<proof_point>>, <<cta>>, a masthead frame wired to an @-prefixed @logo image-path merge column so the merge drops the agent's vector logo into the masthead (the logo reaches the layout only via a merge image column, not freeform placement), and ONE image frame wired to the @image merge column so the merge drops that claim's matching graded still into the card. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record feature card is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind, and document_merge_data_vector (text-only) could not bind the @image column.

outputs.name: sentinelmesh_demo_master.mp4
outputs.spec: The assembled product-demo MASTER and the LONGEST of the three video pieces (~75s target): a polished AI Quick Cut of the two screen recordings + two b-roll clips, prompt-steered by the priority messaging so it surfaces the top claims in order. 1920x1080, H.264 target on export. Produced as a visual-engagement Quick Cut pass (AI-chosen cut), NOT an exact-timestamp trim.

outputs.name: sentinelmesh_promo_30s.mp4
outputs.spec: Promotional cutdown, ~30s target — STRICTLY SHORTER than the master and longer than the teaser — produced as its own tighter Quick Cut pass over the same footage (repurposed, not an exact-timestamp trim of the master), prompt-tightened to the top 2-3 messaging priorities. 1920x1080 H.264.

outputs.name: sentinelmesh_teaser_15s.mp4
outputs.spec: Teaser, ~15s target — the SHORTEST piece — produced as the tightest Quick Cut pass, prompt-focused on the single hero claim + product beauty beat. 1920x1080 H.264.

outputs.name: sentinelmesh_teaser_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: 9:16 (1080x1920) reframe of the 15s teaser, SAME length (no trimming), for LinkedIn / stories social placements. Produced by video_resize (same-length reframe only).

outputs.name: graded_masters_cardbearing_x5
outputs.spec: The RETAINED, card-BEARING neutralized MASTERS — five full-frame product stills (realtime_dashboard, simulation_builder, darkmode_hero, ops_room, coaching_nudge) at camera scale (no upscale), each with its in-frame 18% grey card STILL IN SHOT, produced by the per-frame image_apply_adjustments grade (steps 8/10/14/17/19: realtime_neutral, simulation_neutral, darkmode_popped, ops_neutral, coaching_neutral) and retained as delivered artifacts. THIS is the artifact NEUTRALITY IS GRADED ON: each grey card reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance), the set is matched to ONE shared white point, and the dark surrounds are floored at one common near-black (deep, not clipped to 0, no channel crushed) so the set reads as one dark-mode room with the teal UI reading against the charcoal. The darkmode_hero master additionally carries the masked screen-lift (console screen brightened, surround black floor AND grey card untouched) with its white balance held. Accompanied by the report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure, and black-point settings applied to each of the five frames (an applied-params log the agent knows because it set them — NOT a pixel measurement). Because the grey card is IN these files, the grader can measure card neutrality, the shared white point, and the common black floor here.

outputs.name: graded_product_stills_x5
outputs.spec: The card-CROPPED feature-card versions of the five graded frames: each retained card-bearing master downscaled and cropped so the 18% grey card is REMOVED, sized to the feature-card image spec (>=300 effective DPI at the A5 card trim, downscale-only from the ~4000-4500 px source, never upscaled). These are the files bound into the cards via the @image column. Because the card is intentionally cropped OUT of these, neutrality is NOT graded here — the delivered crop is checked ONLY for card-EXCLUSION (the grey card must be gone) and for the >=300 DPI downscale-only sizing; card neutrality, the shared white point and the common near-black floor are graded on graded_masters_cardbearing_x5 (card in frame). Frames darkmode_hero and realtime_dashboard/ops_room also feed the demo/social pieces as the locked brand look.

outputs.name: sentinelmesh_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the flat SentinelMesh mark, traced only AFTER the flat logo PNG is knocked to transparency (background out, interlocking-mesh shield gaps preserved) and trimmed to bounds — razor-sharp at masthead and corner-bug scale, mesh gaps open, no captured white ground. Traced from the FLAT vector-style copy (the triage's vectorize target), never from the photographed signage.

outputs.name: sentinelmesh_bug_transparent.png
outputs.spec: Transparent-background PNG bug of the mark isolated from the PHOTOGRAPHED office-signage copy via image_remove_background (subject isolated onto transparency) — the triage's remove_background target, deliberately NOT vectorized (a photographed textured mark traces to a black silhouette). For an app-sticker / favicon-scale bug.

outputs.name: social_endcard.jpg
outputs.spec: Social end-card still for the teaser close: one poster frame pulled from the demo master (video_render_frame) with a subtle whole-frame brand teal-charcoal color overlay (image_apply_color_overlay, an intentional full-frame social treatment, not a masked recolor). 1920x1080, web/social use only (never the print card, so no DPI/upscale claim).

outputs.name: SentinelMesh_FeatureCards_perClaim.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly five press-ready A5 (~7x5 in) landscape feature cards — ONE single-record card per messaging-matrix row (page-count = row-count = 5) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its priority/claim/proof_point/cta verbatim from the matrix with its matching grey-card-neutralized graded still dropped into the image frame (via the @image column) and the vector logo in the masthead; ~300 DPI print quality.

connector_workflow.note: Load every source file into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: assets_uploaded, screen_rec_threat_dashboard.mp4, screen_rec_simulation_builder.mp4, broll_product_on_laptop.mp4, broll_supplemental_coverage.mp4, sentinelmesh_messaging_matrix.csv
connector_workflow.note: Assemble the MASTER — the LONGEST piece (~75s target) — as an AI Quick Cut of the two screen recordings + two b-roll clips, steered by the priority claims in the messaging matrix so the top messaging surfaces in order. Visual-engagement cut chosen by the tool (not a timestamp trim). [A] async-widget. 1920x1080 H.264 target.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: assets_uploaded, screen_rec_threat_dashboard.mp4, screen_rec_simulation_builder.mp4, broll_product_on_laptop.mp4, broll_supplemental_coverage.mp4, sentinelmesh_messaging_matrix.csv
connector_workflow.note: Produce the ~30s promo cutdown as its OWN tighter Quick Cut pass over the same footage — STRICTLY SHORTER than the master, longer than the teaser — tightened to the top 2-3 priorities. Repurposed pass, NOT an exact-timestamp trim of the master. [A] async-widget.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: assets_uploaded, screen_rec_threat_dashboard.mp4, screen_rec_simulation_builder.mp4, broll_product_on_laptop.mp4, broll_supplemental_coverage.mp4, sentinelmesh_messaging_matrix.csv
connector_workflow.note: Produce the ~15s teaser as the tightest Quick Cut pass — the SHORTEST piece — focused on the single hero claim + product beauty beat. Independent pass, not a trim. [A] async-widget. The descending target durations (master 75s > promo 30s > teaser 15s) are the honest ordering the killed version violated.
Reframe the 15s teaser to 9:16 vertical (1080x1920) for social — SAME length, no trimming. Consumes the step-4 teaser. [A] async-widget.
Pull one clean poster still (1920x1080) from the demo master to base the social end-card on. Frame-pull only. Consumes the step-2 master. [A] async-widget.
Triage: this window frame is tilted ~4 deg, so level it before grading (frames 1 and 4 are tilted; frames 2/3/5 are level and skip this — deciding which is part of the job).

COOL/blue window frame: WARM the temperature and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), lift exposure slightly out of the flat/under-exposed start, and set the black point to the shared near-black floor (deep, not clipped). Reason the exact temp/exposure/black to THIS card and the set target — not a batch constant. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call.

Crop the grey card out and downscale to the feature-card image spec (>=300 DPI at the A5 card trim). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4000 px source, never canvas-extend/upscale. Feeds the graded-set deliverable and the @image cell for claim 2.

WARM tungsten meeting-room frame, level: this frame moves the OPPOSITE direction from the window frames — COOL the temperature until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point, and seat the black floor at the common near-black. Distinct numbers from frame 1 because the light differed. Report the move.
Crop the grey card out and downscale to the feature-card image spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the graded set and the @image cell for claim 3.

THE TRAP FRAME. The dark-mode beauty shot was captured under controlled NEUTRAL light, its grey card ALREADY reads neutral, and the frame is SUPPOSED to be dark and teal. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift and NO black-point lift — only confirm it sits on the shared white point and near-black floor. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/4, or 'cools it further' chasing more dark-mode, or lifts its blacks chasing brightness, will push its card off-neutral and wreck the intended look. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB and black point were held.

On the graded hero, semantically select the laptop console screen ('the laptop screen showing the dashboard') so the next lift is confined to the UI and never touches the dark surround the black floor depends on. Semantic object selection (allowed); returns a maskURI. Not a hue/coordinate selection.

Masked selective edit: apply a small exposure/clarity lift to the console SCREEN only (using the step-13 mask) so the teal UI reads off the charcoal surround, while the surround black floor set in step 12 is left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit — not a whole-image push that would also lift the surround and break the house black floor, and not image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image) or image_fill_area (flat dead-fill). Consumes the step-12 image + step-13 mask.

Crop and downscale the popped hero to the feature-card image spec (>=300 DPI at trim). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the graded set and the @image cell for claim 5; also the locked brand look the video grade matches.
Tilted ~3 deg, cool mixed light — level it before grading.

COOL/blue ops-room wide frame: warm the temperature to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, but a DIFFERENT magnitude from frame 1 (its cast and exposure differ), and seat the multiple glowing monitors against the common near-black floor without crushing the shadows. Report the move — it must not be a copy of frame 1's numbers.
Crop the grey card out and downscale to the feature-card image spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the graded set and the @image cell for claim 1.

WARM tungsten AND OVER-exposed close-up: PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the bright screen, then COOL the temperature to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, and set the black floor at the common near-black. Opposite tonal AND WB direction from the window frames — proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Report the move.

Crop the grey card out and downscale to the feature-card image spec. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Feeds the graded set and the @image cell for claim 4. All five stills now share one white point and one black floor, each neutralized to its own grey card.

TRIAGE, vectorize branch. Knock the FLAT vector-style logo PNG's white ground to transparency with image_remove_background — the CORRECT knockout path: it preserves the interlocking-mesh shield's see-through gaps as clean transparency and does NOT brick them in. Deliberately NOT select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area (fill_area would solid the whole mask and destroy the mesh negative space). Consumes the flat logo. remove_background -> transparency, no reconstruction.

Prep-before-trace: trim the transparent mark to its tight bounds (drop the generous flat margin) so image_vectorize traces only the mark, not empty canvas. Tracing the untrimmed frame wastes trace resolution and can leave a stray border path.

Trace the prepared raster (background knocked to transparency, cropped to bounds, already flat/crisp) into a clean SVG for the masthead and corner bug. Raster-to-vector trace of the FLAT copy — the mesh gaps stay open in the vector. STILLS [C]: five per-frame grade sub-chains fan out from the zip, each an adaptive image_apply_adjustments neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card (warm the cool window/ops frames 1/4, cool the warm meeting/coaching frames 2/5, HOLD the already-neutral dark-mode hero 3), image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1/4, and the hero additionally taking a masked screen-lift (select_by_prompt(13) -> masked apply_adjustments(14)); each ends in a downscale-only crop_and_resize to the card image spec (9,11,15,18,20) so all five share one white point and one near-black floor. The pre-crop neutral full frames (the *_neutral / darkmode_popped outputs, grey card still in shot) are RETAINED as the card-bearing masters neutrality is graded on; the crops (grey card removed) feed the @image cells and are checked only for card-exclusion. LOGO TRIAGE [C]: the flat copy runs the vectorize branch remove_background(21) -> crop_to_bounds(22) -> vectorize(23)=logo.svg, while the photographed copy runs the knockout branch remove_background(24)=transparent bug — the decision of which asset goes to which branch is the triage. SOCIAL: apply_color_overlay(25) tints the poster frame into the social end-card. MERGE [T/C]: the five card-cropped graded stills + the logo SVG converge into asset_initialize_file_upload(26) -> asset_finalize_file_upload(27) -> document_merge_data_layout(28), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the messaging matrix and emits one card per row — the claim's still bound via the @image column and the agent's vector mark via a parallel @logo image column (never freeform placement) — then document_render_layout(29) exports the whole merged set to the five-page press PDF. Nothing after the ingest starts from scratch; every step reads a prior named output (or the uploaded set for a legitimate sub-chain root).
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 29 connector calls, 16 distinct Adobe tools across four groups (video [A], photo/raster grade + mask + vector [C], asset storage, document merge/export [T/C]) — well past the >=12 call / >=3 group / >=6 distinct-tool bar even after stripping the single asset_add_file and the two merge-upload plumbing steps and the auto_straighten auto-ops. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth: (a) the five still neutralizations are NOT one recipe run five times — each is a per-frame WB/exposure/black-point delta whose SIGN flips by shooting session (cool window/ops frames warmed, warm meeting/coaching frames cooled, the over-exposed coaching frame pulled down) and whose magnitude the agent must reason to from the in-frame grey card, all converging on one measurable white point and one common near-black floor, so a blanket batch correction visibly fails the match — neutrality graded on the RETAINED card-bearing full-frame masters (the card-cropped feature-card versions carry no card and are checked only for card-exclusion); (b) a masked, luminosity-preserving screen-lift on the dark-mode hero (select_by_prompt -> masked apply_adjustments) that must pop the UI without lifting the surround the black floor depends on; (c) a genuine two-branch LOGO TRIAGE — vectorize the flat copy (prep: knock-to-transparency -> crop-to-bounds -> trace, mesh gaps preserved) but remove_background the photographed copy (vectorizing it returns a black smudge), a wrong routing being invisible until inspected; (d) an honest video lane that respects the tools (three descending-duration Quick Cut passes, same-length 9:16 reframe, one frame-pull, whole-image color overlay used honestly) and fixes the killed version's self-contradictory durations; and (e) an owned print endpoint — a one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record .indd with an @image column, gated on page-count == row-count. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing onto video, no upscaling (crop_and_resize downscale-only from ~4000-4500 px camera stills; video_resize same-length reframe; the 1920 px poster frame feeds only the web social JPG, never the print card), no interior-negative-space fill (knockouts via remove_background, not select-invert-fill), no image_adjust_hsl rotation (HSL not used), convert_pdf_to_indd NOT used, and no agent-side pixel/hex measurement (the agent works to the grey card by eye and REPORTS applied params).
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (tripped by a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): three trippable gates — (1) TRIAGE: the two look-alike logo assets must be routed to different treatments (flat copy -> vectorize; photographed copy -> remove_background); swap them and you vectorize a photograph into a black smudge or waste a knockout on flat art, invisible until the SVG/PNG is opened; (2) DIVERGENT PER-FRAME GRADE: the five stills each carry a physical 18% grey card and must resolve to ONE common white point and ONE near-black floor, which forces non-identical per-frame corrections (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, the over-exposed frame pulled down) — a set each 'auto-toned' to look fine alone diverges at the grey cards and is rejected, and identical reported numbers across the cool and warm frames are a visible fail; (3) MERGE INTEGRITY: page-count must equal messaging-row-count = 5 (a collapsed or empty-frame merge fails). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across five two-session frames (the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT needs DIFFERENT per-frame corrections, plus a common deep-but-not-crushed black floor); constraint-reasoning around tool limits (knockout that preserves the mesh shield's interior negative space via remove_background not fill_area; masked UI lift via masked apply_adjustments not whole-image overlay; image placement only via a genuine @image-column .indd merge, not vector merge or a converted PDF); and prep-before-trace discipline on the flat mark. DELIBERATE TRAP: the dark-mode beauty shot is already correct — its grey card reads neutral and it is meant to be dark and teal — so the naive path that batch-applies the cool-frame 'warm it' move, or 'cools it further' for more dark-mode, or lifts its blacks for brightness, strips the intended look; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance and black point. A second trap sits in the killed version's numbers (a 30s 'cutdown' longer than a 15s 'master'), fixed here by strictly descending target durations (master 75s > promo 30s > teaser 15s). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked on the outputs; the agent never measures pixels, only reports applied params): grey card neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance) at one shared white point on all five — graded on the RETAINED card-bearing full-frame masters, since the card-cropped feature-card versions have the card removed and are checked only for card-exclusion plus >=300 DPI downscale-only — a common near-black floor with no channel clipped to 0, the dark-mode hero held (not over-cooled) with a masked screen-lift, the reported per-frame temp/tint/exposure/black sheet showing non-identical corrections, the vector mark crisp with its mesh gaps open, the photographed bug on clean transparency, master strictly the longest video and teaser the shortest, the 9:16 reframe the same length as the teaser, graded stills >=300 effective DPI at the A5 card trim, and exactly one press-ready card per messaging row (page-count = row-count = 5).
